title: Nautical Mile vs Statute Mile vs Kilometre: When 'Mile' Isn't 'Mile'
h1: Nautical mile vs statute mile — the mile is not one unit
description: 1 nautical mile = 1852 m. 1 statute mile = 1609.344 m. Aviation and marine navigation are in nautical; road signs in statute. Difference: 15%.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: The nautical mile is a minute of latitude. The statute mile is a Roman inheritance. Same name, 15% apart.
body: 'Mile' means one of two things depending on medium. On land, 5280 feet. On water and in the air, one minute of arc along a great circle. The two differ by 15% and the units are not interchangeable in navigation.

> 1 statute mile = 5280 ft = 1609.344 m (land)
> 1 nautical mile (nm, NM) = 1852 m exactly (marine, aviation)
> 1 knot = 1 nautical mile per hour = 1.852 km/h
> 1 mph = 1.609 km/h
Statute mile: US and UK road distances, running events. Nautical mile: maritime charts, aviation flight plans, weather radar range. Kilometre: everywhere else.

A 500 NM leg = 926 km = 575 statute miles. Fuel calculation using 500 statute miles would understate distance by 15% — enough to plan a flight that runs out of fuel. Aviation forces NM throughout; conversion happens only for pilot briefings to the public.
Nautical mile = 1852 m. Statute mile = 1609 m. In aviation/marine work, never let them mix.

faqs.q: Is UK nautical mile the same as US?
faqs.a: Since 1970 they are the same 1852 m. Historically the UK Admiralty mile was 1853.184 m.
One minute of arc on a great circle of the Earth. The exact value was standardised for consistency across nations.
